evidence.claim: Seneca Foods' 2025 annual report describes the business as almost entirely food packaging and references private labels, food service, restaurant chains, international, contract packaging, and industrial channels.

Silgan is described as a manufacturer and seller of rigid packaging for consumer goods, with its most recent annual report available through AnnualReports.com; separate company materials describe food packaging and food-container customer use cases.

SPS Commerce says it is an intelligent supply-chain network connecting retail, grocery, distribution, supply, manufacturing, and logistics trading partners, with over 50,000 recurring-revenue customers using its retail network.

SPS Commerce's 2025 Form 10-K describes a global supply-chain network connecting retailers, brands, distributors, manufacturers, and logistics providers, with recurring revenue representing 96% of 2025 total revenue.
Cal-Maine's 2025 Form 10-K states that Walmart Inc., including Sam's Club, accounted for 33.6%, 34.0%, and 34.2% of net sales in fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

Cal-Maine's corporate materials describe it as the largest egg company in the United States and report fiscal 2025 scale of 48.3 million laying hens, $4.3 billion annual net sales, and 1.3 billion dozen eggs sold annually.

node: Private-label co-manufacturing, specialty packaging, and value-tier consumer staples inputs
summary: Layer 1B expansion found four US-listed direct or second-order names tied to retailer private-label/value-tier staples infrastructure: one retail supply-chain compliance platform, two physical capacity/packaging suppliers, and one staple-input asset owner with high Walmart/Sam's Club exposure. The cleanest direct node exposure is Seneca Foods for private-label packaged food capacity and Silgan for rigid consumer-goods packaging. SPS Commerce is a software/integration bottleneck around retailer-supplier compliance rather than manufacturing. Cal-Maine is included as a value-tier staple input/capacity reference because retailer service levels and private-label shell-egg supply can be structurally hard to replace, but its commodity and disease-cycle risks make the thesis less pure.
